body: Could someone with the appropriate permissions please add the `agenda+` label? I'd like to introduce the Image Preview proposal and gather initial feedback at the November 12 WHATNOT meeting. Thanks!

It looks like the only difference between the `preview` attribute and the `previewset` attribute is that `preview` only allows a single preview source to be specified, while `previewset` allows multiple, using a syntax similar to `srcset`? Since there are no backwards compatibility concerns, I would recommend only adding a single attribute, which uses the set syntax. I don't see any downside for authors, since in the current proposal `` and `` appear to have identical behaviour. --- Since you're allowing the preview set to contain things other than plain URLs, you can't reuse the syntax/parsing defined for [srcset attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#srcset-attribute). The syntax/parsing of the preview set will need to be separately specified. It should be specified in such a way that browsers will be able to parse the preview string even if it contains preview kinds that the browser does not support. Given the complexity of supporting CSS colors and the `url()` function, I might suggest specifying a grammar parsed using the CSS parser [Parse a comma-separated list according to a CSS grammar](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-comma-list) steps? --- Would it make sense to distinguish between and separately select preview kinds which are ready immediately/synchronously (e.g. color) and those which require some async work (e.g. fetching/decoding an image)? If the selected preview isn't ready when the browser is doing initial paint, it might be good to allow falling back to a different preview type which is ready.

Thanks for the helpful WHATNOT discussion and comments here! I’ve updated the [explainer](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/ImagePreview/explainer.md) and added an [HTML/CSS comparison](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/ImagePreview/css-html-comparison.md).


- **Scope:** I’ve deferred `previewset`, keeping one preview per selected image branch. Multiple preview resolutions need clearer use cases. cc: [@flackr](https://github.com/flackr) [@kepstin](https://github.com/kepstin)
- **Progressive delivery:** Separate previews can compete with the main image. The explainer recommends omitting them when progressive rendering is adequate; it does not claim a universal performance improvement. cc: [@flackr](https://github.com/flackr)
- **Existing backgrounds:** I’ve clarified the missing integration: automatic handoff, shared object-fitting rules, lazy loading, and source changes. Previews do not determine layout or remain beneath transparent pixels after handoff. cc: [@emilio](https://github.com/emilio) [@noamr](https://github.com/noamr)
- **HTML versus CSS:** The comparison explores a new CSS mechanism with the same browser-managed lifecycle. Please let me know whether it captures your suggestions. I suggest continuing that discussion in [MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers#1440](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/issues/1440)]. cc: [@noamr](https://github.com/noamr) [@emilio](https://github.com/emilio)
- **Styling and timing:** The appendix explores [presentation selectors and styleable image parts](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/ImagePreview/explainer.md#exploratory-css-styling) and [reveal control](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/ImagePreview/explainer.md#exploratory-image-reveal) separately from preview inputs. These remain exploratory; the core preserves progressive presentation. cc: [@emilio](https://github.com/emilio) [@slightlyoff](https://github.com/slightlyoff)
- **Lazy loading and events:** Lazy deferral includes preview fetching and decoding, even for inline previews. Preview processing does not gate the image’s `load` event or independently delay the document’s `load` event. cc: [@emilio](https://github.com/emilio)
- **Parsing and waiting content:** Deferring lists removes the immediate comma-separated parsing concern, though the typed-value grammar still needs specification. Would showing a waiting color through the [styling sketch](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/ImagePreview/explainer.md#exploratory-css-styling), while the preview loads, address the scenario you have in mind? cc: [@kepstin](https://github.com/kepstin)


With these updates and the remaining design questions open for discussion, would you be supportive of moving the proposal to **Stage 1**?

Is this something that should be solved in HTML? The OP states that often authors use the same placeholder across multiple images, the placeholder is effectively presentational, and even the syntax of the proposed attribute is CSS. CSS syntax in an HTML attribute not explicitly framed around CSS tends to be an architectural smell.

And if we lean more heavily into CSS, it has all the primitives that the use case needs!
This works across browsers:

```css
img {
	content: url("placeholder.png");
}
```

What we _don't_ have is a way to only target the image when it is still loading. But that's useful even _outside_ of placeholders, and has already been [proposed](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/7467) and [accepted](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/7467#issuecomment-3492573205) by the CSS WG.

And for placeholders that are specific to the element, authors could always use an ad hoc attribute and `attr()`. The benefit of a standard attribute is that it doesn't require double handshakes so it composes better, but I'm not sure composability around this is a huge need.

And if it later turns out that we do want an actual official attribute, all we need is adding this to the UA stylesheet:

```css
img[preview]:loading {
	content: attr(preview type(<image>));
}
```

CSS includes primitives that get you all of the stated goals:
- Colors: `image(<color>)` (and gradients too!)
- Responsive image selection: `image-set()`
- Transitions via `cross-fade()`
- The light/dark case can just use `light-dark(<image>, <image>)` instead of the duplicate markup in the explainer
- Fetching hints can be done via `url()` modifiers https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1603

Also, the proposed pseudo-elements seem like a more complex and more overfit solution to the same use cases that `@image` was [proposed](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/6807) to solve (also [accepted](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/6807#issuecomment-1248380039) by the WG)
@LeaVerou I thought in a similar direction, but took it a bit further. Interesting to know your thoughts https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/issues/1405
